title: Do You Have to Register a Will in Uttarakhand?
desc: Registering a Will is optional under section 18 of the Registration Act, 1908, but two witnesses must still sign it for it to be valid in Uttarakhand.
why: People in Haldwani and Nainital often delay writing a Will, or pay to register one, in the mistaken belief that an unregistered Will has no legal value.
keyPoints: A Will does not have to be registered; section 18(e) of the Registration Act, 1908 makes registration optional, not compulsory under section 17.
To be valid, a Will must be signed by the person making it and attested by at least two witnesses, under section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925.
Registration does not by itself prove a Will is genuine, but it makes the date and signature harder to dispute later.
A person can instead deposit a sealed Will with the Sub-Registrar under section 42 of the Registration Act for safekeeping.

sections.h: Is it compulsory to register a Will in Uttarakhand?
p: A Will does not have to be registered anywhere in Uttarakhand, including at the Sub-Registrar's office in Haldwani or Nainital. Section 18(e) of the Registration Act, 1908 lists wills among the documents for which registration is optional, unlike the sale or gift of land, which section 17 makes compulsory. A handwritten, unregistered Will is just as legally valid as a registered one, as long as it meets the signing rules set out below.

Many people still choose to register a Will because the Sub-Registrar keeps a copy in official records, which makes it harder for someone to later claim the document was forged or changed. The one-time registration fee is usually small compared to the cost of fighting a dispute over a Will's authenticity after the person who made it has died.

sections.h: What makes a Will legally valid, registered or not?
p: Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 sets the signing rules for an ordinary Will made by a Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist or Jain. The person making the Will (the testator) must sign or mark it, and at least two witnesses must each see the testator sign, or receive a personal acknowledgment of the signature, and then sign the Will themselves in the testator's presence.

These rules apply whether or not the Will is registered. A registered Will that does not meet section 63 can still be challenged in court, and an unregistered Will that does meet it can still be enforced through a succession or probate proceeding.

sections.h: Is there a safer option than registration?
p: Yes. Section 42 of the Registration Act, 1908 lets a person deposit a sealed Will with the Sub-Registrar for safekeeping, without revealing its contents to anyone. The sealed cover is opened only after the testator's death, when an authorised person applies to the Registrar for it.

whatToDo: Sign and date the Will, and have both witnesses write their names, addresses and signatures clearly on it.
Store the original safely, and tell a trusted family member or executor where it is kept.
Consider depositing a sealed Will with the Sub-Registrar's office under section 42 if you want extra safekeeping without registering it.
Take legal advice on your own facts, since a Will affecting land in Uttarakhand must still be followed by mutation (dakhil kharij) of the revenue records after death.

hi.title: क्या उत्तराखंड में वसीयत पंजीकृत कराना ज़रूरी है?
keyPoints: वसीयत का पंजीकरण ज़रूरी नहीं; रजिस्ट्रेशन अधिनियम, 1908 की धारा 18(ई) इसे अनिवार्य नहीं, वैकल्पिक बताती है।
वसीयत मान्य होने के लिए उसे बनाने वाले व्यक्ति के हस्ताक्षर और कम से कम दो गवाहों की उपस्थिति ज़रूरी है, जैसा भारतीय उत्तराधिकार अधिनियम, 1925 की धारा 63 में कहा गया है।
पंजीकरण अपने आप वसीयत को असली साबित नहीं करता, पर इससे तारीख और हस्ताक्षर पर बाद में सवाल उठाना मुश्किल हो जाता है।
व्यक्ति चाहे तो रजिस्ट्रेशन अधिनियम की धारा 42 के तहत सीलबंद वसीयत सब-रजिस्ट्रार के पास सुरक्षित रखवा सकता है।
